$comment: M13. A question page: the approach and the look before he asks (a paragraph of their own), then the body the engine writes (the question, the answer told a family at a time, the thought), then the last word. Holes: approach (where he goes and how he settles; its card may export a prop, 'my hat'), look (his read of them; bind trait for one the last word can bring back), thing (what they have in hand, off their activity card: bind thing; says nothing), body (the question and everything after it; one a sheet). Card holes: prop (place-ambient: bind prop), character (of person, kind look or street). Slots: {person} and {person.he} .He .him .his .His .man .doing .act .sight .hour; {place}, {victim}, {hour}; roles {prop} {trait} {thing}. The close: callback lines bring a role back; plain lines need none; when neither fits, the engine's own last word (M12's close deck, by what the page came to). Never a verdict.

sheets.name: Stool and trade
sheets.notes: The camp golden §3: the approach, the look from the trade, then the question. The look may leave a trait for the last word.

sheets.name: The room first
sheets.notes: A thing in the room gets its sentence before he goes over (or turns back, on a second question), a paragraph of its own, so the page stands somewhere; the last word can bring it back.

callback: When it was over, {person.he} and I both looked at {prop}. It was the only thing in the room nobody had asked anything of.

sheets.name: Hands full
sheets.notes: What they have in hand, said once in the setup (off their activity card), like the golden's pad. The telling's tel-b can bring it back (put down to answer, picked up after); the last word pays the look instead, so the thing is not said four times. The line is written only on a callback page with a thing to bind; otherwise this is the approach and the look.

sheets.name: One more
sheets.notes: A second question the same visit: turned back to, and one line that knows he has already had his turn.

parts.text: {person.He} had hoped one question would be the end of me. Most people do.

sheets.name: A cool welcome
sheets.notes: Somebody guarded, the first question of a visit: the approach, the look, and how little they did to make him welcome. The try after the question is the engine's.

parts.text: {person.He} gave me the kind of welcome people keep for the man who reads the gas meter.

sheets.name: About them, for once
sheets.notes: A question about their own life: the setup says why this one is different before he asks it aloud.

parts.text: I’d been asking people about other people all night. For a change, I wanted to ask one about {person.him}self.
